verdict.evidence: With a non-contiguous (transposed) input or weight, grad_input or grad_weight is wrong whenever the upstream gradient is not exactly 1. In the replayed spec (mean reduction, scalar upstream 0.7, input layout "transposed"), grad_input differs from the float64 oracle by 0.017 at [3,2] (kernel -0.0568, reference -0.0398). That is about 1.7e5 times the allowed error. The loss and grad_weight are fine. The same failure shows for a transposed weight, where grad_weight fails. With upstream ones the check passes, because the rescale is skipped. Contiguous, row_strided, col_strided and offset layouts all passed. A sweep of 192 configs with contiguous tensors also passed. It covered all reductions, label smoothing, z-loss, bias, ignore_index and frozen weight. Cause: grad_input = torch.zeros_like(_input) (line 72) and grad_weight = torch.zeros_like(weight) (line 77) keep the transposed strides of the inputs. The backward rescale then uses element_mul_kernel (called at lines 301-322), which addresses rows as program_id * stride(-2) and reads contiguous columns of length H. For a column-major gradient tensor, that stride is 1, so the wrong elements are scaled. Some elements are scaled several times and others not at all.
